summary: Square wooden lighthouse on Prevost Island's eastern point, lit 1 November 1895; keepers left in 1964 after a fire at the dwelling; Parks Canada owns it, and it is reached only by boat.

structures.type: square pyramidal wooden tower with kitchen attached
small white wooden tower carrying a fog bell
structures.note: Fog bell 900 ft southeast of the light, ready 1 September 1896.

structures.type: keepers' dwelling, attached to the first tower; a detached dwelling from 1949
structures.note: Detached dwelling built 1949 (LighthouseFriends). Destroyed by fire on 3 March 1964.

structures.type: present tower, shorter than its predecessor, with wooden footbridge from helicopter pad

access.note: Prevost Island is mostly private. The lighthouse and Richardson Bay shore are in Gulf Islands National Park Reserve, reached only by private powerboat, sailboat or kayak. Grounds open, tower closed (LighthouseFriends). The station record's 'closed' is narrower than LighthouseFriends' 'grounds open'.

facts.agency: Parks Canada (Gulf Islands National Park Reserve); transferred 2006

events.note: Unmanned stake light set on the point, at the request of George Rudling, captain of the steamer Islander
Square pyramidal wooden tower by G. A. Frost, contract price $870
Fog bell ready 1 September 1896; machinery struck it every fifteen seconds in fog
Seventh-order dioptric replaced by fifth-order dioptric; petroleum vapour illuminant (as the Department's report published in 1912 records)
Vessel stranded off Portlock Point on 28 June 1916 (fiscal year 1916-17 statement); name not legible in the copy read
New dwelling, detached from the tower
Keepers' dwelling destroyed by fire on the evening of 3 March 1964 (LighthouseFriends)
Present tower, shorter than its predecessor
Transferred to Parks Canada, added to Gulf Islands National Park Reserve

corrections.proposed: square pyramidal wooden tower, built 1895, about 14.6 m (48 ft base to vane); present tower built 1987, shorter than its predecessor (height not given in sources read)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1895 is the first light (wooden tower, in operation 1 November 1895). The record's 1987 'built' is the present tower.
The station record's 'Fl W 1s' and OSM's 'Q W' differ from the Coast Guard's list entry 'Q W 1s', which is used here.

notes_for_editor: CONFLICTS: (1) Access: LighthouseFriends says the grounds are open and the tower closed; the station record says 'closed' and quotes the Lighthouse Directory as saying the site is closed to visitors. Story says the tower is closed and the shore is reached only by boat; a current Parks Canada statement would settle the grounds. (2) Keeper Jack Reddy vs Frank Reddy: LighthouseFriends' 1960 article says Frank Reddy; its keeper list says Jack Reddy (1948-1964). Not reconciled. (3) James Heanski: LighthouseFriends dates him 1959-1964 in the keeper list, overlapping Reddy. The 1964 fire details come from LighthouseFriends only; no newspaper or Coast Guard report was read. The story keeps to LighthouseFriends' wording: the keeper's remains were found in the ruins. (4) The 1895 keeper appointment (2 December 1895, $460) is matched by row in the 1901 list, not by name; LighthouseFriends does not give the appointment date. (5) The 1913 G. A. Watson entry is matched by its position in a list (the names column is in a different order from the station column). (6) The 1912 lens change: the Department's report is cited for the change; LighthouseFriends does not mention it. The report is labelled as published in 1912; the fiscal year it covers is not stated in the story. (7) The 1917 vessel's name is not legible in the OCR text read (the names column and the remarks column do not line up); the story gives no name. The year is inferred: the statement covers the fiscal year 1916-17 and the investigation was on 1 July, so the stranding was 28 June 1916. (9) Wikipedia says Portlock Point was automated in the late 1960s; LighthouseFriends says 1964. Wikipedia not cited. (10) Watson's 1914 and 1919 letters are quoted by LighthouseFriends from documents not read; the story paraphrases, except 'a slave pen', which LighthouseFriends quotes. (11) The Department's 1913 diaphone and 1914 works listings mention Portlock Point, but the entries are in multi-column tables; they are not used in the story. (12) Post-1960 keepers (Church, Waugh, Georgenson, Reddy, Heanski) are named as LighthouseFriends prints them. Heanski's details are limited to the 1964 event as LighthouseFriends reports it. FACT-CHECK 2026-10-28 (independent checker): all 48 original quotes were found in their sources on the first run. Story revised: the 'southern Gulf Islands' gloss is removed (LighthouseFriends says 'Gulf Islands'); 'Almost all of Prevost Island is privately owned' is footnoted; the 1919 letter is described as LighthouseFriends describes it (a newspaper article, not a magazine); the 1924 injury and the 1964 fire are told in neutral terms, and the keeper's remains are described only as LighthouseFriends prints them. The 28 June stranding is dated 1916 only as 'most likely': the Wreck Commissioner's entry prints no year, and the text read does not state the fiscal year's end date (31 March 1917 is not confirmed in the copy read). The Department's 1913 list line 'Portlock point G. A. Watson' is read by row order (station followed by keeper, as on neighbouring rows); the page image was not viewed. The 2 December 1895 / $460 appointment (1901 list) and the 1912 illuminant entry are read from the corpus text, not from page images.
